text: What are the two main testing strategies covered in this module?

options.text: Linear and Half-Split testing
Black Box and White Box testing
Unit and System testing
Manual and Automated testing

explanation: The two main testing strategies are Black Box testing (no internal knowledge) and White Box testing (full internal knowledge).

options.text: The tester has full knowledge of the internal code and system structure
The tester has no knowledge of how the system works internally — testing is done purely from the outside
Testing is carried out only by developers
Testing focuses on examining code branches and logical paths

explanation: In Black Box testing the tester has NO knowledge of how the system works internally. Testing is done purely from the outside, looking at inputs and outputs — just like an end user would.

options.text: The tester has no knowledge of the internal system and tests from the outside only
The tester has full knowledge of the internal code and system structure
Testing is done by end users who are unfamiliar with the system
Testing focuses only on the user interface

explanation: In White Box testing the tester has FULL knowledge of the internal code and system structure. Testing is based on examining code statements, branches, paths and conditions.

text: Who typically carries out Black Box testing?

options.text: Developers and technical experts only
End users or testers with no internal system knowledge
Network administrators
Hardware engineers

explanation: Black Box testing is carried out by end users or testers — people who interact with the system from the outside without needing to know how it is built.

text: Who typically carries out White Box testing?

options.text: End users with no technical knowledge
Developers or technical experts with knowledge of the internal code
Helpdesk staff
The manufacturer's sales team

explanation: White Box testing is carried out by developers or technical experts who have full knowledge of the internal code and system structure.

text: What is the focus of Black Box testing?

options.text: Examining code statements, branches and logical paths
Whether the software behaves correctly — looking at inputs and outputs
Checking memory allocation and CPU usage
Verifying that all code comments are accurate

explanation: Black Box testing focuses on whether the software behaves correctly — it looks at inputs and outputs rather than how the system is built underneath.

text: What is the focus of White Box testing?

options.text: Whether the system looks correct to an end user
Code structure and logic — examining statements, branches, paths and conditions
Testing network connectivity
Checking that the user interface matches the design

explanation: White Box testing focuses on the internal code structure — examining statements, branches, paths and conditions to ensure the logic is correct.

text: What level of testing is Black Box?

options.text: Low-level
Mid-level
High-level
It has no defined level

explanation: Black Box testing is high-level testing — it tests the system from the outside without any knowledge of the internal workings.

text: What level of testing is White Box?

options.text: High-level
Mid-level
Low-level
It has no defined level

explanation: White Box testing is low-level testing — it digs into the internal code structure, examining statements, branches, paths and conditions.

text: What other names is White Box testing known by?

options.text: Open Box, Visible Box, Clear Box
Glass Box, Transparent Box, Clear Box
Internal Box, Logic Box, Code Box
Developer Box, Expert Box, System Box

explanation: White Box testing is also called glass box, transparent box or clear box testing — all referring to the fact that the tester can 'see inside' the system.

text: Should a thorough test strategy use Black Box, White Box, or both?

options.text: Black Box only — end user perspective is all that matters
White Box only — code correctness is all that matters
Both — Black Box checks user behaviour, White Box checks code correctness
Neither — automated tools handle all testing

explanation: A thorough test strategy uses both. Black Box checks that the system does what the user expects. White Box checks that the code underneath is correct and covers all logical paths.

text: A tester is checking whether a login form accepts correct credentials and rejects incorrect ones — with no knowledge of the underlying code. Which type of testing is this?

options.text: White Box testing
Black Box testing
Unit testing
Regression testing

explanation: This is Black Box testing — the tester is checking inputs and outputs (credentials accepted/rejected) with no knowledge of how the login code works internally.

text: A developer is checking every branch and condition in their authentication code to make sure all logical paths are covered. Which type of testing is this?

options.text: Black Box testing
White Box testing
Acceptance testing
System testing

explanation: This is White Box testing — the developer is examining the internal code structure, checking branches and conditions, which requires full knowledge of the code.

text: Match each characteristic to the correct testing type.

columnA.text: Carried out by end users or testers
Carried out by developers or experts

explanation: Black Box = no internal knowledge, done by end users/testers. White Box = full internal knowledge, done by developers/experts.
